title: Chained invoker rate safeguards + recursion detector for multi-tool execution
creator: Ava Martin
description: Problem: As we expand multi-tool chaining (function/tool calling + streaming responses + structured outputs) we observe two failure modes in production: unbounded recursion when tools re-invoke the model with overlapping context, and eviction storms where continuous streaming + retries overloads downstream tool endpoints. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight, runtime-level detector + rate-safeguard to keep tool execution loops bounded while preserving composability and structured output fidelity across compatibility layers (old/new SDKs).
background: We have multiple customer incidents where a LLM -> tool -> LLM loop triggered repeated calls (KV cache grew, costs spiked). Existing protections live at the app layer (prompt-level guards) but not at the orchestrator. Concurrently, streaming optimism (client reconnects + automatic retries) amplified tool load. This work complements prior work on prefix/KV caching and the orchestrator's fallback policies.
goals: Detect likely recursion cycles across the tool invocation graph within a single request and gracefully short-circuit with structured error outputs
Apply adaptive rate-safeguards for chains that exceed expected call patterns to downstream tools (backoff + degrade to summary responses)
Maintain streaming contract with clients: ensure partial tokens are emitted when safe and truncated in a structured way when execution halts
Introduce telemetry and dashboards for chain depth, unique-tool-sets-per-request, and rate throttle events
non_goals: Full static analysis of user-provided tool code
Permanent blocking of tool calls across tenants (this is per-request/session enforcement)
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes chain_depth and tool_graph_digest in request traces for every multi-tool invocation
Requests with detected recursion return a 200 streaming closure event containing a structured field 'execution_halted' with reason and safe_summary
Adaptive throttle prevents >N (configurable) downstream tool calls per 30s window per request and logs a throttle_event with sample payload
Integration tests covering: simple chain (3 tools), recursion loop (A->B->A), streaming client reconnect + retry scenario — all pass in CI with deterministic mocks
Dashboard shows decreased repeated-tool invocation rate on the Canary host by >= 45% during synthetic test ramp
design_notes: Detector: compute a small fingerprint (stable bloom/hash) per tool invocation node including tool id, input_digest, and model_version. Maintain a per-request set and abort if the same fingerprint seen > threshold.

Rate-safeguard: token-budget-aware backoff. If downstream service latency or error-rate spikes, switch to 'summarize' strategy where the model is asked to condense pending context into a single call, reducing fanout.
Streaming behavior: emit a final JSON-framed token chunk that contains 'execution_halted': true with a 'summary' field. Keeps client contract stable across SDKs and older API clients.
Compatibility layer: default behavior respects client-specified 'strict_mode' header. For legacy clients without header, server applies conservative defaults documented in migration guide.
Observability: add trace attributes: chain_depth, unique_tool_count, recursion_detected (bool), throttle_applied (bool). Correlate with existing token-cost dashboard.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (3 days): Add fingerprint and per-request set store in orchestrator. Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and threshold behavior.
Phase 2 (4 days): Implement adaptive rate-safeguard flow and summarize fallback. Add streaming termination payload format; update SDKs to surface termination events (minor SDK bump).
Phase 3 (2 days): Integrate telemetry hooks and add dashboard panels. Run synthetic load test against Canary cluster.
Phase 4 (2 days): Rollout gradual canary -> 25% -> 100% with kill-switch. Prepare runbook for incident response.

notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive detection might false-positive on benign repeating tool calls (e.g., pagination). To mitigate we add tool-specific whitelists and allowance windows.
We prefer a runtime, per-request approach to keep overhead low and avoid cross-request state across cached KV stores.
We will not encode business logic in the runtime; only generic summarization and truncation are allowed. App-specific de-duplication remains the app's responsibility.
qa_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint hash stability and threshold crossing
E2E with mock tool endpoints: normal chain, intentional recursion, slow downstream causing summarize fallback
Chaos test: simulate client reconnect + retry loop to ensure streaming closure emitted exactly once
Performance test: measure overhead < 1.5% p95 latency for non-chaining requests
risks: False positives for legitimate repeated calls (e.g., cursor-based APIs) — mitigated by allowlist and per-tool counters
SDK compatibility friction if streaming final event shape changes; mitigated by backward-compatible framing and migration doc
Increased runtime memory per-request for fingerprint set — keep fingerprint small (64-bit) and cap set size
rollout_plan: Deploy to Canary cluster with instrumentation (Canary tag: ENG-88476)
Run 48h synthetic traffic with ramped recursion scenarios
If metrics are stable, move to 25% of traffic for 24h, then 100%
Kill-switch available via feature flag and emergency config to disable summarization/throttles
customer_notes: Planned change will be opt-in for enterprises flagged to avoid surprises during pilot
We will announce in the next customer newsletter and provide a migration guide for strict vs legacy SDKs
